top_choice_rationale: P001 credits the optical lattice clock to Katori (magic-wavelength lattice concept) and Ye (carrying the strontium clock to the 10^-18 accuracy and stability frontier), a clean two-name allocation with no comparable contributor excluded. The result is independently reproduced and surpassed and already used for redshift tests, bounds on varying constants and dark-matter searches. A narrow citation on the magic-wavelength lattice and the 10^-18 regime keeps it distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. P002 is a mature discovery but its three-name credit omits Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, so it ranks second, above no award.
